name: com.faremerald.playforge
description: A gameplay framework modelled on Unreal's Gameplay Ability System: abilities, attributes, effects, tags and items, scheduled by ProcessControl and run through TaskSequence. Requires UniTask 2.5.11, which a package cannot declare because it is a git dependency, so add com.cysharp.unitask, pinned to #2.5.11, to the project's manifest.

samples.description: A battle that plays itself: Blue and Red, eight fighters a side, built from attributes, abilities, effects, cues, projectiles and summons made in code, with health bars and effect boxes over each fighter. It needs nothing beyond PlayForge.

A hero arena: pick one of five heroes and an AI hero or a training dummy to fight, give items and change levels, and fight. Every hero, ability, item, effect and attribute is an asset, and between them they use every asset feature. It needs nothing beyond PlayForge, reads the Input System or the Input Manager, and renders in the Built-in pipeline or URP.
Annotated TaskSequence, synced sequence and group process examples, as code to read. They compiled into the runtime until they moved here.

Recipes for common rules, each built from PlayForge's own assets with no code: a curse that bursts, a counter, a crit, an execute, lifesteal, damage return, can't die, on hit, on kill, and a boss's phase; formulas, Scaler assets named for what they compute, as 1 ÷ (1 + 0.06 × Armor); a starter set, a melee attack, a bolt, a slow and a shield; and feedback on uGUI and TextMeshPro, floating numbers, a hit flash, a hit sound, a status bar, a camera shaker and two cues, with a Sparring scene that plays them. Documentation/RECIPES.md describes the recipes, field by field.
